analyze.title: Analyze

toolHint.crosstab: How two categorical answers relate — with a chi-square test.
toolHint.compare: Does a score differ between groups? t-test, ANOVA or their rank-based versions.
toolHint.correlate: Do two scores move together? Pearson or Spearman, with a scatter plot.
toolHint.paired: Compare two scores from the same people — a paired t-test.
toolHint.reliability: Do several items measure one thing? Cronbach's alpha.
toolHint.matrix: Correlations between several scores at once.
toolHint.prepare: Choose which responses count, recode answers and build scale scores.

crosstab.sig: “{row}” and “{col}” are related: answers to one differ depending on the other. The association is {effect} (Cramér's V = {v}).
crosstab.ns: There's no clear relationship between “{row}” and “{col}” in this data. Any differences you see could be chance.
crosstab.fisher: Fisher's exact test (better for small samples): p {p}.

ttest.sig: {a} (M = {ma}) and {b} (M = {mb}) differ on “{y}”. The difference of {diff} is statistically significant, and the effect is {effect} (Cohen's d = {d}).
ttest.ns: {a} (M = {ma}) and {b} (M = {mb}) don't differ clearly on “{y}”. The difference of {diff} could be chance (effect {effect}, d = {d}).

anova.sig: Average “{y}” differs across {k} groups. The effect is {effect} (η² = {eta}). Highest: {top} (M = {topMean}); lowest: {bottom} (M = {bottomMean}).
anova.ns: Average “{y}” doesn't differ clearly across the {k} groups (η² = {eta}).
anova.welchNote: Group spreads differ (Levene p {p}), so rely on Welch's version: F({df1}, {df2}) = {f}, p {wp}.

mw.sig: {a} and {b} differ on “{y}” (medians {ma} vs {mb}). The difference in rankings is statistically significant ({effect} effect, r = {r}).
mw.ns: {a} and {b} don't differ clearly on “{y}” (medians {ma} vs {mb}; r = {r}).

kw.sig: “{y}” differs across the {k} groups (ε² = {eps}, {effect}). Highest mean rank: {top}.
kw.ns: “{y}” doesn't differ clearly across the {k} groups (ε² = {eps}).

corr.sig: “{x}” and “{y}” move {direction}: a {effect} correlation ({symbol} = {r}). It's statistically significant.
corr.ns: There's no clear correlation between “{x}” and “{y}” ({symbol} = {r}).
corr.negative: in opposite directions (one up, the other down)
corr.regression: Each 1-point increase in “{x}” goes with a {slope} change in “{y}” on average; X explains {r2}% of the variation in Y.

paired.sig: People scored differently on “{a}” (M = {ma}) than on “{b}” (M = {mb}). The average change of {diff} is statistically significant ({effect}, dz = {d}).
paired.ns: Scores on “{a}” (M = {ma}) and “{b}” (M = {mb}) don't differ clearly (average change {diff}, dz = {d}).

alpha.summary: These {k} items form a scale with {band} reliability: Cronbach's α = {alpha} (n = {n}).
alpha.reverse: “{item}” correlates negatively with the rest — it may need reverse-scoring (Prepare data → Reverse).

assumption.independentObservations: Each response is counted once (independent observations).
assumption.expectedCounts: Expected counts: {percent}% of cells below 5 (smallest {min}). The test is reliable when ≤ 20%.
assumption.normality: Scores roughly normal or large enough samples (smallest group n = {minN}).
assumption.normalityVariables: Both scores roughly normal or n ≥ 30 (n = {minN}).
assumption.ordinalOutcome: Uses ranks, so it works for ordinal scales and skewed data.
assumption.pairedCases: Uses the {n} people who answered both.
assumption.linearRelationship: Assumes a straight-line relationship — check the scatter plot.
assumption.monotonicRelationship: Assumes one tends to rise (or fall) with the other.
assumption.sameConstruct: Items should all measure the same idea.
assumption.reverseScored: Negatively worded items should be reverse-scored first.
assumption.listwise: Uses the {n} people who answered every item ({dropped} left out).

mixedMethods.intro: Put what people said next to what they answered. Codes, survey answers and the people behind them, in one place.
mixedMethods.jointTitle: Where the conversations and the survey meet
mixedMethods.jointMeta: {sessions, plural, one {# conversation} other {# conversations}} · {respondents, plural, one {# survey response} other {# survey responses}}
mixedMethods.qualCount: {passages, plural, one {# passage} other {# passages}} · {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}

convergenceHint.both: Codes raised in interviews and in survey answers
convergenceHint.qual: Depth without numbers: the survey can't say how common
convergenceHint.quant: Numbers without depth: nobody explained it in a conversation

mixedMethods.emptyJoint: Nothing coded yet. Code a few transcripts and open survey answers, and this table fills in.
mixedMethods.crossTitle: How people who raised a code answered
mixedMethods.crossHint: Pick a closed question. Each row shows the answers of respondents whose open-text answers carry that code, next to everyone.
mixedMethods.noCodedAnswers: No coded open-text answers in this survey yet.
mixedMethods.crossNote: Groups overlap (one answer can carry several codes) and are often small. Read differences as leads to follow, not as tested effects.
mixedMethods.emptyCross: There's no published survey with closed questions in this project.
mixedMethods.casesHint: {both} of {total} participants appear in both a conversation and the survey. Survey responses are linked to a participant through their personal invite.
mixedMethods.sessionsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No sessions} one {# session} other {# sessions}}
mixedMethods.responsesCount: {count, plural, =0 {No survey} one {# survey} other {# surveys}}
mixedMethods.noCodes: Nothing coded for this person yet.
mixedMethods.emptyCases: No participants in this project yet.

create.questionnaireHint: Generate a draft from your research brief, upload a spreadsheet, or start from a template below and build it by hand.

generateHint.questionnaire: Drafts questions from your research questions, hypotheses and proposal (Write-up → Brief). You review and edit everything before publishing.
generateHint.guide: Drafts sections, questions and probes from your research questions and hypotheses. Replaces the current guide.
generateHint.responses: Made-up answers for testing the charts and statistics. They're labelled as generated and you can delete them all at once.
generateHint.participants: Made-up people with example.com emails and a few attributes, for trying things out. Nothing is ever sent to them.
generateHint.codebook: Proposes codes and definitions from your research questions and the text you've collected. Codes you already have stay.
generateHint.transcript: A made-up conversation built from the interview guide.

uploadHint.questionnaire: One row per question: page, type, question, options (separated by |) and more. Download the example to see every column.
uploadHint.guide: One row per question: section, minutes, goal, question, probes (separated by |) and a note.
uploadHint.responses: One row per response, one column per question (use the question text as the header). The example file has your exact columns.
uploadHint.participants: Name, email, phone and id columns are recognised; every other column becomes an attribute.
uploadHint.codebook: One row per code: code, parent, definition and color (1 to 8).

manualHint.questionnaire: Pick a template or a blank form and build it question by question.
manualHint.responses: Opens the form in a new tab. Each submission is saved as a manually entered response, for example from a paper questionnaire.

manualButton.responses: Open the form for data entry

create.uploadedWithErrors: Imported {count}; {errors} rows or cells were skipped

panel.responses: Add data: generate, upload or enter by hand

create.generatedBanner: {count, plural, one {# response is} other {# responses are}} generated test data and included in the results.

reportBuilder.title: Reports
reportBuilder.intro: Put charts, quotes, themes and your write-up together, then share a link, print to PDF or download Markdown.
reportBuilder.empty: No reports yet. Generate one from your data, or start blank.
reportBuilder.emptyReport: This report is empty. Add a block below.
reportBuilder.notePlaceholder: Add a note under this chart (optional)
reportBuilder.shareHint: Anyone with the link can read the report. It always shows current data. Turn it off to revoke the link.
reportBuilder.deleteBody: The report and its public link go away. Your data stays.
reportBuilder.missing: This item was deleted or isn't available anymore.

aiSettings.title: AI
aiSettings.subtitle: Connect Claude to draft questionnaires, guides, codebooks and written analyses, suggest codes and summarise sessions.
aiSettings.statusHint: Keys are encrypted before they are stored and never shown again. Text you send to AI goes to Anthropic.
aiSettings.keyHelp: Create one at console.anthropic.com → API keys. Leave empty to keep the current key and only change the model.
aiSettings.ownersOnly: Only workspace owners can change the AI key.
aiSettings.placeholderNote: Owners and developers can also choose Placeholder next to each Generate button: Lyze's built-in, offline generator, useful for testing without spending tokens.

checkResult.unreachable: Couldn't reach Anthropic from the server

apiSettings.title: API & webhooks
apiSettings.subtitle: Read your data from other tools, and get told when something happens.
apiSettings.keysHint: Read-only access to this workspace's projects, studies and responses.
apiSettings.copyNow: Copy this key now. It won't be shown again.
apiSettings.webhooksHint: Lyze POSTs a JSON event to your URL, signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the X-Lyze-Signature header.
